Test "Choice Experiment: Time‑Saving vs Status Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey presenting two product descriptions of a hypothetical lawn and garden tractor, each emphasizing a different value proposition: (1) time‑saving multipurpose tool with integrated attachments; (2) status‑enhancing design and brand prestige. Participants indicate willingness to pay a premium (percentage above a baseline price) and choose which description they would select. The test is run with 300 U.S. homeowners recruited via an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and region. Each participant sees one of the two descriptions.. Sample: 300 U.S. homeowners, recruited via an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and region.. Measure: 1) Willingness to pay premium (percentage above baseline price) for each description. 2) Choice: which description they would select (Time‑Saving vs Status).. Predictions: T1: Participants will show higher willingness to pay and select the time‑saving description, because they value multipurpose functionality and are willing to pay a premium for integrated tools.; T2: Participants will show higher willingness to pay and select the status description, because they value social prestige and are willing to pay a premium for distinctive design and brand reputation.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay premium for the time‑saving description exceeds the premium for the status description by at least 10 percentage points (e.g., 20% vs 10%), we conclude T1 is better supported. If the status description premium exceeds the time‑saving premium by at least 10 percentage points, we conclude T2 is better supported. If the difference is less than 10 percentage points, the evidence is inconclusive.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Predictions: T1: Condition A will show higher purchase intent, WTP, and status appeal than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will show higher purchase intent, WTP, and status appeal than Condition A.. If Condition B’s average purchase intent exceeds Condition A’s by at least 1.5 points and the difference is significant, we conclude T2 is better supported. If neither condition meets the 1.5‑point threshold, the test is inconclusive and we recommend. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.
